verdict.statement: BOTH mechanisms are real. The 1PN prediction matches the population-level offset (median p* = 0.630 vs predicted 0.630, difference consistent with zero), but it is flat in elongation (rho = +0.05, p = 0.68) and therefore cannot carry the elongation trend: p* declines with axis ratio even after partialling out the prediction (partial rho = -0.26, p = 0.021). The 1PN term sets the central displacement of the exponent; a distinct elongation-dependent (finite-width) effect pulls the most-elongated events back toward 3/5. Neither categorical attribution alone is correct.
